item.title: TCU fires football coach Sonny Dykes, per reports
item.description: Four years after leading the Horned Frogs to within one win of a national championship, Sonny Dykes is out as TCU's football coach. (LM Otero/AP Photo/LM Otero) TCU has fired head football coach Sonny Dykes , according to multiple reports Sunday. Dykes was dismissed after a 38-17 loss to No. 2 Utah on Saturday that dropped the Horned Frogs to 5-6 and 3-5 in the Big 12. Since reaching the College Football Playoff championship game in 2022, TCU has gone 28-21. Dykes is the second Big 12 coach to be fired this season, joining Baylor's Dave Aranda. It was not immediately known if Dykes will coach the Horned Frogs in Thursday's regular-season finale at Texas Tech. Dykes went 41-23 in his five seasons at TCU, with his first year being the high-water mark, a 13-2 campaign that included the school's first berth in the CFP (when the field was four teams) and a victory over Michigan in the semifinals before a blowout loss to defending national champion Georgia in the title game. Prior to his time at TCU, Dykes coached five years at SMU (30-18), four seasons at Cal (19-30) and three years at Louisiana Tech (22-15). Dykes, the son of legendary former Texas Tech coach Spike Dykes, also was an assistant at his alma mater Tech as well as Kentucky, Arizona, Northeast Lousiana and Navarro College. item.title: Camara to continue with Haas for final two races
item.description: It was announced in October that Rafael Camara will be joining Haas for the 2027 season [Getty Images] Brazilian Rafael Camara will continue to race for the Haas team for the final two grands prix of the Formula 1 season. The 21-year-old, who was already signed to drive for the US-based team in 2027 , was drafted in for this month's Sao Paulo Grand Prix after Frenchman Esteban Ocon was dropped following a bust-up with team boss Ayao Komatsu. The decision to keep Camara in the Haas seat in preparation for next season means he will likely lose the Formula 2 title. He is leading the F2 championship by seven points from Bulgarian Nikola Tsolov heading into the final two events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Komatsu said: "We're excited to be able to finish the season with Rafa driving and build on his first two race starts with the team in Brazil and America. "I'm delighted that Rafa's embraced every track session as a learning opportunity and embedded himself further within the team. "We now get to finish the season together which is advantageous to us all ahead of a relatively short off-season and as our 2027 preparations get under way." A statement from Haas announcing the move did not include a quote from Camara. item.title: PSG plan to sign new forward in winter to compensate injury absences
item.description: PSG plan to sign new forward in winter to compensate injury absences Paris Saint-Germain have seen their autumn take a nightmarish turn. Having already been assured that they would be without Kvicha Kvaratskhelia (25) for several months following a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee sustained against FC Barcelona in late October, the reigning double European champions suffered a further blow on Saturday when Désiré Doué (21) sustained the same injury during the Parisians’ away match at Nice. These are two massive setbacks for the Red and Blues, whose aim of winning the Champions League for the third consecutive season has inevitably taken a serious knock. And in an attempt to keep their hopes of a remarkable feat alive, the Parisian management intend to make the most of the upcoming winter transfer window to strengthen the squad. As reported by Le Parisien , several attacking players are reportedly under consideration. These are players with clearly defined characteristics and a versatile profile – primarily wingers – capable of unbalancing defences and winning one-on-one duels, as well as being comfortable in tight spaces. Whilst the exact identities of the targeted players have not been revealed, neither AS Monaco’s Paris Brunner (20) nor AFC Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi (20) are believed to feature in the plans of Luis Campos, with the Parisian sporting director seeking to invest sensibly, without splashing the cash. item.title: Cleveland Browns: Run game has a chance to get rolling after the bye
item.description: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have struggled on offense in several areas this season, and the rushing game is no exception. As the Browns use the bye week to rest up for the final seven games of the season and a potential playoff run, the numbers from the run game are not pretty. Running back Quinshon Judkins leads the team with a meager 423 rushing yards, followed by quarterback Deshaun Watson with 266. Judkins is averaging just 3.4 yards per rush, not exactly what you want to see from your top running back, and has six games with fewer than 50 rushing yards. It’s not all Judkins fault, of course, as the offensive line has taken time to coalesce with five new starters, and opposing defenses are not exactly afraid of the pass game, which makes it that much harder to run the ball. The good news is that the final seven games provide ample opportunity for the Browns to get the run game in gear as they will face some of the league’s worst run defenses. Let’s run through the teams the Browns will be facing to see where they currently rank* when it comes to stopping the run: Week 12 vs. Las Vegas: 1,511 rushing yards (ranked No. 31) and 13 rushing touchdowns allowed (tied for No. 21) Week 13 & 18 vs. Cincinnati: 1,115 rushing yards (ranked No. 20) and 8 rushing touchdowns allowed (No. 16) Week 14 vs. Atlanta: 1,191 rushing yards (ranked No. 26) and 10 rushing touchdowns allowed (tied for No. 18) Week 15 vs. New York Giants: 1,094 rushing yards (ranked No. 18) and 7 rushing touchdowns allowed (tied for No. 11) Week 16 vs. Baltimore: 1,059 rushing yards (ranked No. 15) and 14 rushing touchdowns allowed (tied for No. 30) Week 17 vs. Indianapolis: 1,478 rushing yards (ranked No. 30) and 10 rushing touchdowns allowed (tied for No. 18) As the weather starts to turn colder, the Browns are going to need their running game to function at a higher level if they hope to stay in the playoff race in the AFC. The schedule is set up well for them to accomplish that goal, which would also help open up the passing game and provide the “explosive plays” that have been missing for most of the season. item.title: How skipping shootaround helped the Spurs beat New Orleans
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox (4) drives down the court during an NBA game against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) De'Aaron Fox wandered into the Spurs' locker room late Saturday night after a 114-91 victory over New Orleans , trying his best to stifle a yawn. He failed miserably. In the midst of the busiest month on the Spurs' schedule, Fox was hardly alone in feeling the effects of a long NBA grind. "When you've been through this for a few years, you get used to the course of an NBA season," Fox said. "There's no excuses. Most teams go through this. It's what it is being an NBA player." For the Spurs, Saturday's contest marked the 12 th in a string of 17 games in 30 days, stretching back to Halloween night win over Minnesota. The Spurs have not had more than two days off in a row since Oct. 25 and 26. They will not earn another such breather until Dec. 1 and 2. The climb continues Monday with a game at Sacramento, followed by a Thanksgiving Eve clash against Portland. The taxing schedule makes the Spurs' 10-1 mark in November all the more impressive. "We know what we're building towards," forward Keldon Johnson said. "Each and every game, we focus on that game. We don't look forward and we don't look back. We just stay present in the moment." Coach Mitch Johnson has done his best to help the Spurs navigate the most rigorous portion of their calendar, both physically and mentally. Johnson eschewed the traditional morning shootaround before Saturday's game against the Pelicans to give his weary players a few extra hours to themselves. It was a move Johnson pulled from former coach Gregg Popovich's old playbook. "We've tried to be mindful of (players') time," Mitch Johnson said. "Time is a very important part of our program, and Pop used to talk about it a lot. We try to not waste it." By giving his team an occasional mental break, Johnson hopes he can get more out of them once the game tips off. "I think in contrast to (the rest), we need their energy," he said. "They've done a good job of giving us that." Even so, Mitch Johnson concedes every team goes through a stretch of the season in which coaches and players believe the NBA schedule makers are out to get them. November has been the Spurs' turn. "I think no matter what part of the schedule, you find something to be disgruntled about," Mitch Johnson said. item.description: Northwestern Field Hockey (22-2, 7-1 B1G) walked into the Trager Stadium in Louisville Sunday as the favorites to win the national championship for the third time in a row. The Wildcats walked out victorious with a 3-1 win over Maryland (21-3, 7-1 B1G). Northwestern was given the one seed in the tournament, and breezed through Saint Joseph’s 5-0 in the first round before winning two shootouts in a row against UNC then UConn to make it to the championship game. The Maryland Terrapins were the only team left to stand between head coach Tracey Fuchs – the only D1 coach in history to lead a team to six national championship games in a row – and her 24th tournament win. But even 39th year head coach Missy Meharg could not stand against the Wildcats. The game started with energy and both teams fought for a trip into the circle within the first 90 seconds. Maryland’s pass didn’t connect and fell out of bounds, while the Maryland defense took the ball off the stick of Olivia Bent-Cole. Kiera Sack almost opened up scoring in the 14th minute of play with a lofted pass across the face of the goal. Raquel Hofmeister got a stick on the ball, but her redirect rattled off the right post. The ‘Cats exited a feisty first quarter with zeroes across the board. There was just one shot in the quarter. Feliz Kuhne entered the second quarter with a fast pass across the frame of the goal in search of Babs van Hest who came short by about a foot, even though she had beat her defender to the spot. Maryland maintained possession for the next few minutes and in that time, Northwestern’s Sol Martinez was shown a green card. She entered the circle with a cutback to beat the leading defender and then scored low to the far side while falling down to give Northwestern a 1-0 lead. This time it was Ilse Tromp, but her shot was deflected again. Northwestern recovered at the 25 yard line and Ashley Sessa threw the ball into the circle. Aerin Krys found the ball at the far post and scored her first goal of the entire season, giving the ‘Cats a 2-0 lead, a familiar position for a Wildcats team that had led 2-0 against UConn for almost ten minutes in the semifinal before the Huskies scored two in the last five minutes of the game to extend it to overtime. Our first question of the week, as always, is whether or not you think the Vikings are moving in the right direction. Strangely enough, when you pair an actual, honest-to-goodness, functioning National Football League offense with the NFL’s best offense, fans start feeling a whole lot better about things than they had previously. We are now up to 89% of Vikings fans who feel that the Vikings are moving in the right direction, which is a new high for this season. Honestly, after what we saw against the Packers last week, it’s hard to blame anyone for feeling optimistic about this team, isn’t it? They broke the 30-point mark for just the second time this season, they completed the sweep against a hated rival, and it looks like they have a new lease on life going into one of the biggest games of the year. Speaking of that game, our other question this week had to do with how everybody feels about tonight’s big matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. It seems like a lot of people believe that the Vikings have a pretty good chance in a game that could serve to give them the upper hand in the race for the #1 overall seed in the NFC playoff race. Of those who responded to our poll, a full 70% believe that the Vikings will emerge victorious. We had 45% who think that the Vikings will win in a close one, by a margin of somewhere between 1-8 points, and another 25% who believe that they will win by more than a touchdown (and a two-point conversion). Only 30% of our respondents believe that the Vikings will take the “L” in tonight’s game, with 18% thinking the Vikings will lose by less than a score and 12% believing that they’ll lose by more. Honestly, as we’ve been saying all week, with this defense and, now, with an actual competent offense, this team can hang with. . .and beat. . .any team in the National Football League. The Niners are very impressive on offense, certainly, but the only thing that’s been shown to be able to slow down the Vikings’ defense this season is time of possession. If the Vikings’ offense can stay on the field, sustain drives, and keep the defense fresh, our squad can come out of this one at 8-2. item.title: Boston Celtics President Brad Stevens preaches patience with Mitchell Robinson
item.description: Fans of the Boston Celtics are understandable concerned about the start of new big man Mitchell Robinson, the former New York Knicks center looking like much less of a player than the man who helped will his former ball club to an NBA title this past summer. The Western Kentucky alum, in his defense, did have a shorter offseason due to that title run, but his conditioning (or more accurately, its absence) is only part of the problem behind him tying career lows in scoring (5.1 points per game) while setting a new low for rebounding (5.4 boards per game). "You can tell it's a transition for him, and that's not all that atypical for guys," said Celtics President of Basketball Operations Brad Stevens via CLNS Media ahead of a Sacramento Kings game the Louisiana native was given off for rest. "And so, again, it's so early that we'll see how this all plays out." "But I trust that what he does when he's at his best will translate because it always has, right?" added the Celtics president in a vote of confidence that might leave some fans unsatisfied in the face of Boston's eventual 97-96 loss to the Kings, now the second-worst team in the NBA after said defeat. "I think that getting him to the rim on both sides of the floor, getting him to be in that area where he can be most impactful is something that we'll continue to work on," suggested Stevens, "continue to put him in position where hopefully he can soar with his strengths." And given Boston only took 5 shot attempts in the restricted zone against one of the teams that has defended that part of the court the worst this season, Boston needs Robinson to soar with those strengths more than ever. On Sunday in the national championship game, hopes were high for the Terps to not only win their ninth national title but to end the eight-game losing streak against their fierce Big Ten rival. However, the Terps couldn’t crack the code. A second-quarter landslide from the No. 1-seed Wildcats built the foundation, and a strong defensive effort locked down their fourth national title — and their third in a row — with a 3-1 win. The first half was played at a track-meet pace as the two teams sprinted up and down the field. Each offense hoped to use its speed in transition, but the two defenses hustled back well to thwart threats. Northwestern had the first chance to break the deadlock late in the first quarter. Raquel Hofmeister deflected a centering pass towards the cage, but the ball glanced off the near post to keep the contest scoreless through the end of the first frame. Physicality was also a theme in the first half. Players often bumped bodies and took tumbles in transition and in the tight shooting circle. Northwestern was whistled for a green card early in the second period when Sol Martinez cut down Ella Beach, but the Terps failed to capitalize. Maryland had a few opportunities early in the second period but couldn’t convert. Babs van Hest had the best look when the ball bounced her way in front of the net, but she couldn’t make proper contact. Northwestern used its speed to take the lead midway through the second period. item.title: Schremmer Admits Lying After LPGA Disqualification
item.description: Apr 1, 2025; Evans, Georgia, USA; Scarlett Schremmer, of Ala., tees off No. two during the practice round of the Augusta National Women's Amateur at Champions Retreat. Mandatory Credit: Katie Goodale - Augusta Chronicle/USA TODAY NETWORK Golf demands honesty even when no one is watching, yet University of Miami sophomore Scarlett Schremmer chose to lie, costing her a spot in the field. The college star received a sponsor’s exemption to The Annika tournament last week, a rare chance to show her skills against the best women in the world. Her debut took an unexpected turn Saturday when the LPGA Tour disqualified her for using a green-reading book that violated Model Local Rule G-11. Schremmer had already missed the cut before the disqualification was announced. Model Local Rule G-11 applies to LPGA Tour competitions and limits players to the yardage book approved for that particular event. Schremmer initially told officials she had not used the illegal book, a claim she later admitted was false. The Fear That Drove the Lie The reason for the deception is as simple as it is human. Schremmer confessed in a statement shared on Instagram Stories on Friday, Nov. 20, that she panicked when questioned. She wrote, “I had no idea that I had a yardage book with illegal Information. When I was approached about it, I was scared, embarrassed, and made an extremely poor decision in saying it was not in use.” The book itself was allowed in college golf, which explains why it was in her bag, but it carries no weight on the professional tour. Her mother, former LPGA player Patricia Ehrhart, served as her caddie during the event, adding another layer of personal pressure. Apr 2, 2025; Evans, Georgia, USA; Scarlett Schremmer, of Ala., chips onto No. 11 green during the first round of the Augusta National Women’s Amateur at Champions Retreat. Mandatory Credit: Katie Goodale – Augusta Chronicle/USA TODAY NETWORK A Confusion of Partners and Rules The situation turned messy before the final ruling came down. Professional playing partner Perrine Delacour publicly questioned the tournament’s handling of the situation in a comment on an Instagram post by golf personality Ryan French. Delacour posted on X, according to Yahoo Sports , “Can we talk about the yardage [book] illegal and LPGA trust the sponsor invite over 2 LPGA players and 2 caddies.” She later confirmed to Golfweek that she had spoken directly to rules officials about Schremmer’s use of the book. The LPGA Tour stated that Schremmer violated the rule requiring players to be limited to approved books throughout their round. After photo evidence emerged showing Schremmer using the book during competition, the LPGA disqualified her. She had previously denied using it when questioned by officials. Regret and the Path Forward Schremmer’s admission on Friday marked a shift from denial to accountability. She stated in her post, according to Yahoo , “I deeply regret that, I always will, and I want to own that mistake.”

Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics suffered a frustrating loss on Saturday night, falling 97-96 to the Sacramento Kings despite holding a 13-point halftime lead. The defeat marked Boston’s third consecutive loss. According to Spotrac’s NBA reporter Keith Smith, the Celtics could have avoided it with better lineup decisions from head coach Joe Mazzulla . Smith criticized Mazzulla for resting Jayson Tatum, Derrick White, and Mitchell Robinson against a Kings team that entered the game with a 1-14 record. Boston had two days off before Saturday’s matchup and was coming off consecutive defeats, making the decision to sit key players a questionable one in Smith’s eyes. “This loss was very avoidable by Boston,” Smith wrote. “You don’t rest guys coming off two days off AND consecutive losses. Back-to-back or not, there’s no reason for that. Respect your opponent. Joe Mazzulla got cute with lineups once again. This is starting to become a bad trend.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Celtics entered the game at 11-4, but Tatum, White, and Robinson were unavailable. Tatum was rested, White was dealing with a left AC joint contusion, while Robinson was sidelined with an illness. Boston still appeared to be in control at halftime, leading by 13 points. However, the Celtics completely fell apart in the third quarter, getting outscored 35-13 while going 0-for-13 from the 3-point range. Their shooting struggles continued throughout the night, as they finished 34-for-101 from the field and 13-for-58 from beyond the arc. The Celtics missed 45 3-pointers, setting a franchise record. Paul George and Payton Pritchard led an undermanned lineup, but Boston struggled to find consistent offense. The Celtics also failed to make enough plays defensively down the stretch, allowing Sacramento to capitalize and complete the comeback. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
